victim.name: Chef Basil Thorne
victim.public_summary: Celebrity pastry chef and head judge of the Little Marlow Bake-Off, found slumped over the judging table after tasting the final entry.

content_tags.label: Playing the murderer
content_tags.description: Your character may secretly be the culprit and must keep it hidden all night.

content_tags.label: Romance storyline
content_tags.description: Your character has a (fictional, non-physical) romantic history with another character.

content_tags.label: Lying in public
content_tags.description: Your character must tell at least one scripted lie when questioned in front of the group.

content_tags.label: Solo performance moment
content_tags.description: Your character has a short scripted moment in front of everyone (e.g. a speech).

roles.name: Ollie Finch
roles.public_bio: Two-time runner-up and the village's most determined amateur baker. Entered a lemon tart this year.

private.backstory: Basil Thorne humiliated you on live radio two years ago, calling your tart 'a lemon-scented apology'. Your shop has struggled ever since.
secrets: You added a large dose of your grandmother's sleeping tonic to the judge's tasting slice of your tart.
You borrowed the gardener's shed key on the morning of the bake-off and never returned it.
private.goal: Win the bake-off and make sure nobody learns what was in that tart.

roles.name: Dot Marsh
roles.public_bio: Editor, reporter and photographer of the Little Marlow Gazette. Never without a notebook.

private.backstory: The Gazette is close to folding. A scandal at the bake-off would be the story that saves it.
secrets: You have been quietly blackmailing the judge over a plagiarised cookbook and he paid you twice.
private.goal: Get the scoop first, and keep the blackmail out of print.

roles.name: Hal Briggs
roles.public_bio: Keeps the village green immaculate. Grumbles about marquee pegs in his lawn.

private.backstory: You have tended the green for thirty years and know every path behind the marquee.
secrets: Basil Thorne was your half-brother; nobody in the village knows you are related.
private.goal: Find out who did this, without revealing your family connection.

roles.name: Prudence Vale
roles.public_bio: Chair of the bake-off committee. Gives the welcome speech every year, whether asked or not.

private.backstory: You booked Basil Thorne as judge for the publicity, and because you were once engaged to him.
secrets: You and Basil were secretly engaged twenty years ago; he broke it off the night before the wedding.
private.goal: Keep the bake-off's reputation intact, and your old engagement out of the gossip.

roles.name: Rupert Lyle
roles.public_bio: Flamboyant newcomer to Little Marlow and this year's favourite. Talks about his 'patisserie journey' at every opportunity.

private.backstory: You moved to the village a year ago and have been desperate to be accepted. Winning the bake-off would make you a local legend.
secrets: Your showstopper entry was bought from a London patisserie and re-boxed in your kitchen.
private.goal: Keep your cake's origins hidden and win the crowd's sympathy.

roles.name: Pip Thorne
roles.public_bio: Basil Thorne's long-suffering personal assistant and nephew. Carries his clipboard, his umbrella and his grudges.

private.backstory: Your uncle promised you'd take over his cookery column. Last week he gave it to someone else.
secrets: You have been forging your uncle's signature on paid product endorsements for months.
private.goal: Make sure nobody looks too closely at your uncle's paperwork.

roles.name: Dr Imogen Hale
roles.public_bio: The village GP, called from the cake stall when the judge collapsed. Calm, precise and slightly terrifying.

private.backstory: You have looked after most of the village for fifteen years and know more of its secrets than anyone.
secrets: Years ago you prescribed a strong sleeping tonic to Ollie Finch's grandmother, and you never asked for the leftover bottles back.
private.goal: Work out what caused the collapse without your old prescription coming to light.

roles.name: Mabel Crisp
roles.public_bio: Runs the village shop and post office. Sold every contestant their lemons, and remembers who bought what.

private.backstory: Gossip is the real currency of your shop, and today is the best day of trade you've had all year.
secrets: You sold the cream for the judging table a week past its date and relabelled it.
private.goal: Hear every bit of gossip, and keep the cream out of the conversation.

roles.name: PC Wendy Hart
roles.public_bio: Little Marlow's only police constable, technically off duty and judging the jam category.

private.backstory: You have waited your whole career for a real case, and you'd rather solve it before the detectives arrive from town.
secrets: You'd had two pints of cider at the beer tent and left the tasting tent unwatched for twenty minutes.
private.goal: Crack the case yourself before anyone notices your lapse.

roles.name: Councillor Bertie Fenwick
roles.public_bio: Parish council chairman, presenter of the trophy and enthusiastic wearer of the ceremonial chain.

private.backstory: You love a ceremony and a captive audience, and you've been working up the courage to ask Prudence Vale to dinner.
secrets: You have been writing Prudence Vale anonymous love poems and slipping them into the committee minutes.
private.goal: Keep the day dignified, and finally get a moment alone with Prudence.

relationships.description: Ollie has made it very clear they think you're a fraud. They're not entirely wrong.
Your uncle and employer. Demanding, ungrateful, and about to cut you out.
You treated Ollie's grandmother until she passed away last winter.
The woman you've admired for years. She has never once noticed.
He mocked your baking on the radio. You have never forgiven him.
Dot wrote a kind article about your shop last spring. You like her, but she asks too many questions.
Your secret source of income, and your best story.
Your former fiancé. You told the committee you'd never met before.
